body.statement:
The literal coordinatewise no-wider requirement has a finite-sample valid
fallback. In the spectral-split calibration handle, take the measurable
covariance envelope to be the constant function \(K_\Sigma\), and define
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)=\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal R}_n=\mathcal R_n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h=\mathcal C_n^h.
\]
Then every coordinate interval is no wider than its deterministic
\(K_\Sigma\)-box counterpart with probability one, the moment region has
finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over the compact
class, and the rational encoding and exact semialgebraic inverse are
preserved. This construction certifies equality of widths; the frozen
handle is not used here to claim a strict adaptive improvement.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq3\) and a law \(P\) in
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})\).  Equip
the trajectory space \(\Omega_n=\mathbb R^{(n+1)d}\) with its Borel
\(\sigma\)-field and define
\[
 \widehat K_{\Sigma,n}:\Omega_n\longrightarrow(0,\infty),
 \qquad
 \widehat K_{\Sigma,n}(w):=K_\Sigma.
\]
This map is measurable because, for every Borel set
\(E\subseteq(0,\infty)\), its inverse image is \(\Omega_n\) if
\(K_\Sigma\in E\), and is empty otherwise.

Let \(\Sigma_{n,P}=\operatorname{Cov}_P(W_n)\).  The explicit uniform
coarse spectral-density resolvent bound in
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\), under the restrictions
collected in \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\), gives
\[
 0\preceq\Sigma_{n,P}\preceq K_\Sigma I_{(n+1)d},
 \qquad
 \|\Sigma_{n,P}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K_\Sigma=\widehat K_{\Sigma,n}(W_n)
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Thus the constant measurable envelope dominates the trajectory covariance
uniformly over the compact class.

It is also admissible for the spectral splitting specified by
\(\mathrm{def{:}adaptive\mbox{-}calibration\mbox{-}handle}\).  Indeed, for
a symmetric lag-moment matrix \(H_{\ell ij}\), let
\(H_{\ell ij}=H_{\ell ij}^{+}-H_{\ell ij}^{-}\) be its spectral
positive-negative decomposition, where
\(H_{\ell ij}^{+},H_{\ell ij}^{-}\succeq0\).  For
\(s\in\{+,-\}\), covariance domination and congruence imply
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(H_{\ell ij}^{s}\Sigma_{n,P})
 =\operatorname{tr}\!\left((H_{\ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}
 \Sigma_{n,P}(H_{\ell ij}^{s})^{1/2}\right)
 \leq K_\Sigma\operatorname{tr}(H_{\ell ij}^{s}),
\]
and submultiplicativity gives
\[
 \bigl\|\Sigma_{n,P}^{1/2}H_{\ell ij}^{s}
 \Sigma_{n,P}^{1/2}\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \|\Sigma_{n,P}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \|H_{\ell ij}^{s}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K_\Sigma\|H_{\ell ij}^{s}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Thus both spectral parts are controlled by the constant envelope;
recombining them recovers the deterministic two-sided calibration already
certified by \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\).

Define, for every realized trajectory,
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha):=\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal R}_n:=\mathcal R_n,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h:=\mathcal C_n^h.
\]
For each \((\ell,i,j)\in\{0,1\}\times V\times V\), the corresponding
coordinate interval is therefore exactly
\[
 \operatorname{Out}_N\!\left((\widehat M_\ell)_{ij},
 2K_\Sigma\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(4d^2/\alpha)}{n}}
 +\frac{\log(4d^2/\alpha)}{n}\right\}\right),
\]
the deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) interval of
\(\mathrm{def{:}moment\mbox{-}box}\).  Thus every fallback coordinate
width equals, and hence is no larger than, its deterministic counterpart at
every sample point.  In particular,
\[
 P\!\left\{\text{all fallback coordinate widths are no larger than their
 deterministic-\(K_\Sigma\) counterparts}\right\}=1.
\]
Moreover, equality of the moment regions and
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\) yield
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}}
 P\{(M_0,M_1)\in\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^M(\alpha)\}
 =
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}}
 P\{(M_0,M_1)\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\]
Every endpoint is rational by the defining property of
\(\operatorname{Out}_N\).  Finally,
\(\widetilde{\mathcal R}_n=\mathcal R_n\) leaves all polynomial equalities
and inequalities in \(\mathrm{def{:}inverse\mbox{-}region}\) unchanged,
and \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n^h=\mathcal C_n^h\) leaves the transfer
projection unchanged.  Hence the rational encoding and exact branch-free
semialgebraic inverse are preserved.  By
\(\mathrm{thm{:}global\mbox{-}honest\mbox{-}inversion}\), the same
equalities also preserve finite-sample transfer coverage.  Since every
width comparison is an equality, no strict adaptive improvement is claimed.
